theses.title: The one-paragraph story
theses.text:
## The one-paragraph story

Loading rules as prose does not scale: once roughly 140 accumulated feedback
rules ride along, a fresh session starts near 400–500k tokens of always-on
context, where rules fire wrongly or vanish when needed most. In the project's
RPG vocabulary, that is bringing the **whole stash into every map** — as if a character
carried gear for every damage type when the encounter called only for cold
resistance. In plain language, irrelevant rules consumed attention and created
unintended interactions before the task began. The author's implementation
answers with _compiled_ rules: each correction becomes a typed mechanism (a
permission, a guard, a reactor, an evaluator, a transformer, a workflow gate)
attached only where relevant. A session in that profile gets **a build, not a
biography** — one active behavior, a handful of linked supports, its selected
safety layer, and the exact task state. The platform supplies the compiler and
mechanism contracts without prescribing that loadout. The [starter proof](../evidence/WO-118/README.md) completed resident-owned scratch delivery and review repair with writer replacement and resident restart; a fresh export demonstrated live status, while efficiency remains unmeasured.

theses.title: The core bet
theses.text:
## The core bet

> "The true work of the inventor consists in choosing among these combinations
> so as to eliminate the useless ones... the rules that must guide the choice
> are extremely fine and delicate. It's almost impossible to state them
> precisely; they must be felt rather than formulated." — Poincaré, via Pirsig

Generation is cheap and getting cheaper; the scarce asset is the **selection
function** — the operator's sense of what is good, currently exercised one
correction at a time. DotLn's bet is not that this delicate judgment can be
exhaustively formulated. It is that useful operational approximations can be
progressively arrived at: source incidents preserve what was felt, candidate
mechanisms approach it from different directions, and regression fixtures show
where each construction agrees or diverges. As mathematical or geometric
techniques can converge on a shape without becoming the shape itself, the
formulation is an instrument for approaching the operator's selection function,
not a claim to contain it precisely. **The model changes; the organization
survives.** Claude, Codex, a human, a shell script, and a future model are
interchangeable occupants of the same actor slot.

That bet needs an excellent foundation before it needs a long feature list. In
the reference implementation, the smallest useful loop—declare intent, see what
the system understood, observe authorized progress, receive timely feedback,
and inspect evidence—should already feel responsive, legible, and worth
repeating. Competitive gap-filling does not excuse a weak loop. When another
system introduces a useful idea, DotLn first asks whether the exact behavior can
be accommodated by existing primitives, compositions, ports, and runtime
lowerings. If not, the difference becomes evidence for one missing primitive or
boundary, not permission to bolt on an opaque special case. Integration and
semantic accommodation are preferred to imitation; both preserve every
capability contract the receiving implementation declares and expose any
omitted or lossy capability.

theses.title: The differentiated interface
theses.text:
## The differentiated interface

DotLn's second thesis is about _authoring_, not running:

> "I will take the entire Business, Leadership, and Personal Development shelf
> at Barnes & Noble and just map them to different agent / subagent
> communication structures... at once anyone who has read those books is an
> expert in some feature of the app — and it turns all those books into
> programming books overnight."

The analogies are not documentation — **the analogies are the ways you mix and
match the agents**. Every pattern (5S, the Ladder of Leadership, mitigated
speech, Theory of Constraints, commedia dell'arte roles, the
Algorithms-to-Live-By policies) compiles into exact mechanics, and the same
compiled program renders through an open-ended set of isomorphically equivalent
views: an RPG character with a Path-of-Exile-style socket-and-link build, a
business pattern card, a statechart, a function table, a marble/Morse temporal
track, a TypeScript DSL, an event timeline. Friendly metaphors are authoring
languages, never camouflage: every view either provably compiles to the same
normalized program or is labeled a lossy projection with the exact mechanics one
click away.

### Shape-first synthesis

The operator uses situations and analogies to communicate a desired **shape**: a
relationship, interaction, transition, contrast, feedback loop, or felt quality.
Literal similarity to the reference is not the acceptance test unless a specific
literal detail becomes load-bearing. Preserve the experience first, then
progressively lower it through observable interaction, domain mechanics,
contracts and evidence, and finally technology selected from representative
environment evidence. An imperfect analogy can carry a precise requirement;
source accidents do not become ontology by resemblance.

This is the standing interpretation rule for earlier and future operator
ideation. Its fullest product expression is the first-party application thesis,
[`προτείνω`](11-protino.md), but it applies to the whole platform.

theses.title: Three horizons, one kernel
theses.text:
## Three horizons, one kernel

1. **Work operating system** — workstreams, disposable workers, evidence-backed
   completion, offline-capable state, a near-empty main thread. The immediate
   product.
2. **Executable pattern workshop** — the shelf-to-mechanism compiler and the
   drag-a-card-onto-an-agent authoring surface. The differentiated product.
3. **Agent ecology & simulation laboratory** — paired counterfactual runs,
   first-divergence detection, agent swaps, reflection-policy experiments over
   recorded event logs. The research product.

Horizon 3 must emerge from the same kernel (deterministic replay is what makes
counterfactuals possible at all) and is not allowed to distort Horizon 1.
The [workstream application candidate](12-workstream-application.md) develops
Horizon 1 through concrete end-user journeys and gradual workflow replacement,
including one outcome spanning multiple repositories. It leaves deployment and
application identity open and does not allocate another release rung.
[`προτείνω`](11-protino.md) is the operator-named application destination that
joins Horizons 2 and 3: prose-authored patterns and ad hoc interventions become
playable inside an inspectable counterfactual community. Naming the destination
does not move it ahead of the release ladder or make its application-local
content kernel doctrine.

theses.title: Mission — increase the chance of operator flow
theses.text:
## Mission — increase the chance of operator flow

This is the mission of the author's personal implementation and a motivating
use of the platform, not a compulsory objective or operating policy for every
DotLn owner.

AI-assisted work commonly falls into a babysitting mode: the operator repeatedly
restates context, supplies procedural guidance, coordinates tools and workers,
checks unsupported completion claims, recovers stalled work, and spends active
attention on the machinery instead of the idea. The desired alternative is not
unbounded improvisation or confidence without evidence. It is a sustained
creative flow in which the operator can keep the idea and implementation
direction in mind while the surrounding work behaves dependably.

The reference implementation's mission is to improve the conditions for that
**operator flow state**.
Supporting research, capability-building, coordination, routine procedure,
recovery, and verification should happen automatically when authorized,
predictably when routine, and helpfully when a genuinely material decision needs
the operator. Product and research investment should favor capabilities that
remove recurring supervision and avoidable context switches without exporting
their cost into correctness, authority, evidence, privacy, or recoverability.

The implementation cannot promise or infer a person's psychological state. It can
reduce interruption, repetition, manual ceremony, and rediscovery; preserve
intent and working context across handoffs; package necessary interruptions as
decision-ready inputs; and make recovery unsurprising. Under its selected
profile, flow does not silently authorize scope expansion, skipped verification,
perpetual action, or self-certification. “Give an agent a build, not your
biography” remains useful architectural shorthand for one mechanism serving
this larger mission.

exclusions.text:
Not an agent, an agent harness, or an agent-orchestration layer, as its
  identity. DotLn is an **agentic platform**: the shared substrate on which
  people and software actors hold work, authority, and evidence. It contains an
  orchestration layer and hosts harnesses as observed environments
  ([runtime primitive catalogs](03-architecture.md#runtime-primitive-catalogs)),
  but neither of those is what it is.
Not a prompt library, and not a wrapper that makes one vendor's model nicer.

Not a prescribed catalog of ideal agents, roles, personalities, workflows, or
  organizational doctrine. Bundled patterns are examples and optional starting
  points, not kernel truth.

Not dependent on a public marketplace. Local files, private catalogs,
  organization-internal registries, and offline or air-gapped installations
  remain complete authoring and distribution paths.

Not one prescribed autonomy curve. Presence and recorded time are policy
  inputs; an explicit owner policy may hold, shrink, grow, peak, reset, or loop
  scope and authority within its declared ceiling.

In the reference implementation, not a metrics theater: no invented numbers,
  no activity-as-progress, evidence precedes "done," and utilization is not the
  objective. A profile that omits verification says so instead.

The reference implementation is not finished when it works for its author:
  v2.0.0, the roadmap's Teammate-ready rung, means a person who has never read
  these docs can declare a bounded intent and receive a verifiable result
  ([the rung's number](../evidence/WO-276/decisions.md#wo-276-d073--this-orders-release-is-v100-and-the-roadmaps-teammate-ready-rung-is-v200-on-the-operators-word)).

orders.title: WO-297 — A day's figure that is reached ends no turn (version assigned at activation)
orders.objective:
A session in a root that declares a daily figure is told,
once the figure is reached, that it is reached and that no turn ends for
it. The executor's root no longer tells an executor to end its turn when a
prompt's facts say so. Everything else about the day's line and about the
standing file is as it was.
orders.cost:
changes one sentence of the day's line and its comment, the
opening of one executor rule (four bytes fewer in the executor's root, by
the texts below), the expected text of three cases, one row of a generated
rule table and one passage each of the kit guide and product 07. Removes,
from every prompt of an instance that declares a daily figure and has
reached it, the instruction to end the turn.
`packages/skeleton/src/observed-facts.ts` and
`packages/skeleton/src/loadouts/contributor.ts` are registered evidence
sources: the editions they stale are re-minted with `npm run sync`. No file
of `FEEDBACK_SOURCE_PATHS` is edited. One complete review run at handoff.
Wall-clock, tokens and steps are unknown until run.

criteria.text:
At or above a figure, the day's line says that the figure is reached
   and that no turn ends. Supported input: the use and figure a root's
   `docs/control/budgets.json` and its sessions give. Command:
   `npm test -- --only harness-fixtures`, the day's-line case of
   `scripts/test-observed-facts.mjs`.

   | Given | Then |
   | --- | --- |
   | a figure in tokens and a day's use equal to it | the line ends with the Design's sentence and does not hold `end the turn` |
   | the same figure and a day's use below it | the line holds neither `The daily figure is reached` nor `ends no turn` |

   Control: the first row fails at the base, where the line ends with the
   sentence that holds `end the turn`. The second fails where the sentence
   is appended whatever the use.

The prompt hook delivers that line. Supported input: a prompt in a
   fixture root whose day's use has reached its figure. Command:
   `npm test -- --only harness-fixtures`, the case of
   `scripts/test-harness.mjs` that reads a prompt's facts.

   | Given | Then |
   | --- | --- |
   | the fixture of that case, with 1,650 tokens used of a figure of 1,650 | the day's line among the facts the hook returns ends with the Design's sentence |

   Control: the row fails at the base.

The executor's emitted root no longer ends a turn at a day's figure.
   Command: `npm test -- --only skeleton`, the case of
   `packages/skeleton/test/executor-supports.test.ts` that reads the
   emitted roots.

   | Given | Then |
   | --- | --- |
   | the emitted `dotln-executor` root under `.claude/skills` and under `.agents/skills` | each holds `A day's figure` and ``finish the step in hand, write `docs/evidence/WO-NNN/standing.md` and end the turn`` |
   | every emitted role root | none holds `say the day's figure is reached` |

   Control: the second row fails at the base, and so does the first on its
   first text.
`npm test -- --review`, `npm test` and `npm run test:docs` pass.

finishes the time limits. When it closes, the kit launches its critic by
name and its critics' points come back to planning by class; a planning
pass launches the critic of the critics; a paired review round is one
command; the discovery bound says what ran out; no time limit in the kit

orders.title: WO-291 — A target order starts from its base branch's tip, and its heading claims no version (version assigned at activation)
orders.objective:
An instance's planner writes which repository an order
changes and nothing about commits. When the order starts, its worktree
stands on what the repository's base branch holds then, the control log
records that commit, and every later step reads the recorded commit as it
does today. A planner who needs a named commit can still write one. A
target order's heading says nothing that will never happen, and a session
that changed an order's judged bytes is told which line and how to put it
right.
orders.cost:
adds one fetch of the target clone's base branch to a target
order's start, bounded by a row of the table of limits and never a stop;
one admitted form of the `Repository:` line and its readers' handling of
it; one advisory; about eleven cases. Removes the amendment an
instance's operator authorizes today each time an order's pinned base has
gone stale, and the hand edit of a heading that says a version is coming.
`scripts/resume.mjs`, `scripts/worktree.mjs`, `scripts/work-orders.mjs`,
`scripts/lib/target-worktrees.mjs` and `scripts/lib/plan-receipts.mjs` are
declared sources of the `harness-fixtures` or `plan-refutation` suite. No
file of `FEEDBACK_SOURCE_PATHS` is edited. One complete review run at
handoff. The fetch's measured time on core's host is recorded in the
decisions before and after; wall-clock, tokens and steps are otherwise
unknown until run.

criteria.text:
`worktree start` of a fixture target order starts its worktree at the
   commit this table gives. Supported input: a registered repository's
   clone and an order carrying either line. Command:
   `npm test -- --only target-worktree`.

   | Given | Then |
   | --- | --- |
   | the unpinned line, and the clone's `origin` holding two commits on the base branch that the clone lacks | the worktree's `HEAD` is `origin`'s base-branch tip after the fetch |
   | the unpinned line, and a fetch of `origin` that exits non-zero | `HEAD` is the clone's remote-tracking base branch as it stood before the start |
   | the unpinned line, and a fetch of `origin` that outlasts the limit its row sets (the fixture's `time-limits.json` sets that row to one millisecond) | `HEAD` is the clone's remote-tracking base branch as it stood before the start |
   | the unpinned line, and a clone with no `origin` | `HEAD` is the clone's local base branch |
   | the pinned line, and the base branch moved past that commit | `HEAD` is that commit |
   | the first row's fixture, with the clone's `remote.origin.uploadpack` set to a program that leaves a marker file and a hook under its `core.hooksPath` that leaves one | `HEAD` is `origin`'s base-branch tip, and neither marker file exists |

   Control: the first four rows and the sixth fail at the base, where the
   unpinned line is refused as malformed. The fifth passes there and must
   still pass; it fails under the planted fault that the start resolves
   the tip whatever the line holds. After the change the sixth fails
   under the planted fault that the start runs the clone's own
   `git fetch`.

The start records the commit it resolved, and an activation with no
   start to take a base from says so. Command:
   `npm test -- --only target-worktree`.

   | Given | Then |
   | --- | --- |
   | the first row of criterion 1 | the activation event's base commit and the registry entry's base each equal that tip |
   | an order with the unpinned line and no started target worktree, and `npm run resume -- activate` | it exits non-zero, the control log gains no event, and its message holds `worktree start` |

   Control: both rows fail at the base, the second because the base
   refuses the line itself and its message does not hold `worktree start`.

A start that cannot fetch says so once and goes on. Command:
   `npm test -- --only target-worktree`.

   | Given | Then |
   | --- | --- |
   | the second row of criterion 1 | the start exits 0 and prints exactly one advisory line, which holds the start commit's full id and its committer date in ISO 8601 |
   | the third and the fourth rows of criterion 1 | the same |
   | the first row of criterion 1 | the start prints no such line |

   Control: the first two rows fail at the base. The third fails under the
   planted fault that the advisory prints on every start.

The board's base column shows what is known. Command:
   `npm test -- --only work-orders-fixtures`.

   | Given | Then |
   | --- | --- |
   | an open member order with the unpinned line | the column shows the registered base branch's name |
   | a member order activated from the unpinned line | it shows the commit its activation recorded |
   | an open member order with the pinned line | it shows the commit the line names |
   | a member order activated from the pinned line | it shows the commit its activation recorded |

   Control: the first two rows fail at the base. The last two pass there
   and must still pass.

A never-activated order is withdrawn with what its line declared.
   Command: `npm test -- --only resume`.

   | Given | Then |
   | --- | --- |
   | a never-activated order with the unpinned line, and `npm run resume -- withdraw` | it exits 0, and the control log's withdrawal event holds the repository's id and no base commit |
   | a never-activated order with the pinned line, and the same command | the event holds the id and the commit |

   Control: the first row fails at the base. The second passes there and
   must still pass.

A derived order against a repository is written with no version
   placeholder. Command: `npm test -- --only derived-orders`.

   | Given | Then |
   | --- | --- |
   | a derived contract for a registered repository | the heading the kit writes for its order does not hold `(version assigned at activation)` |
   | a fixture target order whose heading has no placeholder, and `worktree start` (`npm test -- --only target-worktree`) | the start exits 0 and the control log holds its activation event |

   Control: the first row fails at the base. The second passes there and
   must still pass.

`release prepare` on a target order changes nothing and says so.
   Command: `npm test -- --only release-preparation`.

   | Given | Then |
   | --- | --- |
   | a target order's worktree, and `npm run release -- prepare --local` | it exits 0, `git status --porcelain` prints nothing afterwards, and the output holds `target order records no release; no files changed` and `the order's heading stays as filed` |

   Control: the row fails at the base on the second text.

The refusal of changed order bytes names the line and both routes.
   Command: `npm test -- --only plan-refutation`.

   | Given | Then |
   | --- | --- |
   | a fixture order whose judged heading was edited to a label that is not a version, and `npm run plan -- check` | it refuses, and its message holds the order's path, the changed line's number, `restore the judged line` and `npm run plan -- amend-order` |

   Control: the row fails at the base, where the message names neither the
   line nor a route.

A malformed line is refused with both forms named. Command:
   `npm test -- --only work-orders-fixtures`.

   | Given | Then |
   | --- | --- |
   | an order whose line is `**Repository:** <id> @ abc` | the reader refuses, and its message holds `expected **Repository:** <id> or **Repository:** <id> @ <40-or-64-hex-base-commit>` |

   Control: the row fails at the base, whose message holds
   `expected **Repository:** <id> @ <40-or-64-hex-base-commit>` and no
   `or`.
`npm test -- --review`, `npm test` and `npm run test:docs` pass.

orders.nonGoals:
changing what any later step computes from the recorded
base; rebasing or refreshing a worktree that has already started; a
refusal of a stale pin; the version assignment of a self order; rewriting
any filed order; the target's publish, gate or close.

orders.title: WO-294 — Main works on an order's worktree whatever its configuration holds, and a drive starts from a checkout off main (version assigned at activation)
orders.objective:
The operator types `drive: WO-NNN` and the drive starts,
whatever keys the order's own configuration has gained and whatever branch
the primary checkout is on. The integration that a final review runs from
main works on the same order. A checkout still refuses an unknown key in
its own configuration when its own commands load it.
orders.cost:
adds one reader of a checkout's roots, its use at the lookups
that cross from one checkout's code into another's files, one branch in the
order-worktree lookup and about six cases. Removes, for each drive during a planning pass, the operator's switch of
the primary checkout back to `main` or a run of the phases by hand, and
for an order that adds a configuration key the drive, the status and the
integration that refuse. `scripts/lib/config.mjs`, `scripts/lib/order-worktrees.mjs` and
`scripts/lib/target-worktrees.mjs` are declared sources of the
`configuration-root` or `harness-fixtures` suite. No registered evidence
source's judged behavior and no file of `FEEDBACK_SOURCE_PATHS` is edited.
One complete review run at handoff. Wall-clock, tokens and steps are
unknown until run.

criteria.text:
A status read from the main checkout reaches such an order. Command:
   `npm test -- --only harness-fixtures`.

   | Given | Then |

   Control: the row fails at the base, where the lookup refuses the key.

A drive from the main checkout launches such an order's phase. Command:

   Control: the row fails at the base.

Main's integration script works on such an order. `integrate` works on
   the checkout it is run in, and the roles run main's copy of the script
   in the order's worktree. Supported input: the suite's fixture with no
   authored conflict (its option `authored: false`, as the instance cases
   use), with the two names in the order worktree's configuration and

   `npm test -- --only worktree-integration`.

   | Given | Then |
   | --- | --- |
   | that fixture, and the main checkout's `scripts/worktree.mjs integrate WO-NNN` run with the order's worktree as its working directory | it exits 0, and `main`'s tip is an ancestor of the order's branch |

   Control: the row fails at the base, where main's script loads the
   worktree's whole configuration to build a path (`docRelative`) and
   refuses the key.

A status read finds its control plane when no worktree holds `main`.
   Command: `npm test -- --only harness-fixtures`.

   | Given | Then |
   | --- | --- |
   | a fixture whose primary checkout is on another branch and in which no worktree holds `main`, and `node scripts/drive.mjs status WO-NNN` run in the primary checkout | it exits 0 and prints the order's phase |

   Control: the row fails at the base, where the command prints that no
   main-branch control-plane worktree was found.

A drive starts when no worktree holds `main`. Command:
   `npm test -- --only harness-fixtures`.

   | Given | Then |
   | --- | --- |
   | the fixture of criterion 4, and a drive with the fake host | the fake host receives one launch of the phase the order's status names as next |

   Control: the row fails at the base.

A checkout's own commands still refuse an unknown key in its own
   configuration. Command: `npm test -- --only configuration-root`.

   | Given | Then |
   | --- | --- |
   | a checkout whose own `dotln.config.json` holds an unknown section key, and `node scripts/harness.mjs check` run there | it exits non-zero and names the key |

   Control: the row passes at the base and must still pass. It fails under
   the planted fault that the strict loader takes the roots reader.
`npm test -- --review`, `npm test` and `npm run test:docs` pass.

any change to what a checkout's own commands refuse in its

orders.title: WO-289 — A session is told to go on, and ends its turn only for what the operator must do (version assigned at activation)
orders.objective:
A session that has been dispatched keeps working until its
dispatch records its completion. It puts a choice of route to the operator
as a recommendation it then follows, it reads steering when the operator
sends it, and it ends a turn to wait only where the operator said to pause
or stop, where a refusal or the host names something only the operator
can do, or where it waits on a task of its own with nothing else to do.
The texts the kit gives a session at the moment of choice (a role's root,
the dispatch briefing, the context a hook adds to a prompt, an advisory,
the pause the operator opens with `analysis:`) all say so, and none of them
says the opposite. A message the operator sent while a turn was running
reaches the session marked as written without the reply that followed it. An owner who wants sessions to check in more removes
the rule, as any rule of the author's.
orders.cost:
rewrites one rule of the author's layer, `blocked-turn`, in the
six role roots that carry it, about three lines more in each; changes the
text of two executor supports, three briefing and context lines, three hook
messages, one shared rule and the sentence on the operator's controls; adds
one line to the context of a message sent while a turn was running, one
branch to the operator-control reader and about twelve cases. Removes from every executor dispatch the
instruction to offer a turn boundary before each queued action, and from
every later prompt of a session in analysis the instruction to pause again.
`packages/skeleton/src/loadouts/contributor.ts`,
`packages/skeleton/src/loadouts/executor-supports.ts`,
`packages/skeleton/src/stops.mjs`, `packages/skeleton/src/harness-host.ts`,
`packages/compiler/src/harness.ts` and
`packages/compiler/src/operator-control.mjs` are registered evidence
sources: the editions they stale are re-minted with `npm run sync`. No file
of `FEEDBACK_SOURCE_PATHS` is edited, so no feedback re-mint or live
episode is owed. On `main` the executor's, the reviewer's and the planner's
roots stand 57, 75 and 12 bytes under their cold-start ceilings (the cost
table's drift series); in WO-288's worktree, measured on 2026-11-23, they
stand 3,267, 2,722 and 263 bytes over. So the executor records each root's
bytes before and after and removes at least what it adds, the supports'
removed words and the old rule's sentence first; a root over its ceiling at
handoff is named there with its measure and boarded as a follow-up, as
product 07's Discipline has it, and no acceptance is recorded. One complete review run at handoff; a
second at final review only if the integrated identity moved. Wall-clock,
tokens and steps are unknown until run.

criteria.text:
After `node scripts/harness.mjs emit`, each emitted role root says of
   ending a turn what this table gives it
   (`npm test -- --only harness-fixtures`).

   | Root | Says |
   | --- | --- |
   | `dotln-executor`, `dotln-verifier`, `dotln-reviewer`, `dotln-release-close`, `dotln-planner`, `dotln-refuter` | under the rule `blocked-turn`: take the route you recommend in the same turn where it lies within the dispatch's scope and the session's authority, and end a turn to wait for three reasons only, which are the operator's pause, stop or cancel, a block that a refusal or the host names as the operator's alone, and a task of the session's own with no other step left |
   | `dotln-router` | state once what only the operator can clear, with the one line that clears it, and none of the clauses of the row above |

The executor's root and its dispatch briefing tell it to announce its
   intent in one line and go on in the same turn, and neither holds the
   words "steering opportunity" or "turn boundary"
   (`npm test -- --only process-debt`).

With `question-pathways` equipped, the context the prompt hook adds to
   an unprefixed question is the emitted role sentence on answering the
   operator, word for word (`npm test -- --only compiler`).

In a root where the stop advises, the messages of `live-gate`,
   `dispatch-bound` and `worker-cap` each open with what was observed and
   that the call went on, and none tells the operator to authorize, wait
   or run a command (`npm test -- --only harness-fixtures`).

The rule `dispatch-bounds`, in each of the six roots of criterion 1's
   first row, says that where the bound's message is an advisory the work goes on
   (`npm test -- --only harness-fixtures`).

In a session where `analysis:` is on and no `operator override:` is
   open, a prompt does to the analysis what this table says
   (`npm test -- --only harness-fixtures`).

   | The prompt | Result |
   | --- | --- |
   | `resume: next`, `planning:`, `ideation:` or `drive: WO-NNN`, a case for each | ends the analysis, and the prompt gets the role context it gets in a session that never entered analysis |
   | `resume: status` or `resume: times`, a case for each | leaves the analysis on |

While `analysis:` is on, the message each hook gives after the entry
   prompt (a later prompt's context, a tool hook's message and the Stop
   hook's) says that analysis is on and names `analysis: off`, and does not
   hold the words "Pause the current routine"
   (`npm test -- --only compiler`).

The context the prompt hook adds to an operator's message is as this
   table says (`npm test -- --only harness-fixtures`).

   | What the hook can read when the message is sent | The context |
   | --- | --- |
   | the session journal holds a prompt of this session and no Stop row after it, and the host's transcript holds no interrupt after that prompt | holds one line that gives the time the message was sent, says that a turn was running then and says that a reply sent after that time was written without it |
   | the same journal, and the host's transcript holds an interrupt after that prompt | holds no such line |
   | the journal holds a Stop row after the session's last prompt, or no earlier prompt of the session | holds no such line |
   | the journal or the transcript cannot be read | holds no such line |

Each of these says that analysis ends at a dispatch or at
   `analysis: off`: `CLAUDE.md`; `scripts/kit/CLAUDE.template.md`; the
   sentence on the operator's controls in each emitted root that carries it
   (`dotln-executor`, `dotln-verifier`, `dotln-reviewer`, `dotln-planner`,
   `dotln-refuter`, `dotln-router`); and
   `docs/product/07-execution-guide.md` under "Operator recovery controls"
   (`npm test -- --only harness-fixtures`; `npm run test:docs`).
`npm test -- --review`, `npm test` and `npm run test:docs` pass.

orders.title: WO-290 — A turn that leaves a dispatch unfinished goes on once (version assigned at activation)
orders.objective:
A session dispatched to execute, repair, verify or review an
order does not sit idle between the operator's visits. When it ends a turn
with its dispatch unfinished, and it is not waiting on a task of its own,
on a plan's approval or under a pause the operator opened, the kit sends it
back to work once, with a reason that names what is unfinished. The session
then goes on, or says in one line what only the operator can do and ends
its turn, which the kit then lets it do.
orders.cost:
adds one decision to the Stop hook, one feature and its default,
one reason text and about eight cases; adds to a session that stops early
one continued turn, whose tokens are unknown until run. Removes the
operator's prompt to a session that stopped with its dispatch unfinished
and the idle time before it, 43 minutes in the one case the record times
(WO-288-D168); how often that recurs is not measured.
`packages/skeleton/src/harness-host.ts` and
`packages/skeleton/src/observed-facts.ts` are registered evidence sources:
the editions they stale are re-minted with `npm run sync`. No file of
`FEEDBACK_SOURCE_PATHS` is edited. One complete review run at handoff.

criteria.text:
With the feature on, the Stop hook's output for each state below is as
   the table says (`npm test -- --only harness-fixtures`). "Unfinished"
   means a journaled `resume: next`, `resume: fix`, `resume: verify` or
   `resume: final review` whose completion the order's control log does not
   hold.

   | State when the turn ends                                                         | The hook                            |
   | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------- |
   | Unfinished, and none of the rows below holds                                     | prevents the end and gives a reason |
   | Unfinished, and the host reports the turn as already continuing from a Stop hook | lets it end                         |
   | Unfinished, and a background task of the session is running                      | lets it end                         |
   | Unfinished, and the order's route stops at `awaiting-plan-approval`                              | lets it end                         |
   | Unfinished, and `analysis:` or `operator override:` is on                        | lets it end                         |
   | The dispatch's completion is recorded, or the session holds no such dispatch | lets it end |
   | The session's journal or the order's control log cannot be read | lets it end |

The reason the hook gives names the order's id and the dispatch phrase
   and says both courses: go on by the route the session would recommend,
   or say in one line what only the operator can do and end the turn
   (`npm test -- --only harness-fixtures`).

With `"features": {"continue-unfinished-turn": false}` the hook lets the
   turn of the table's first row end
   (`npm test -- --only harness-fixtures`).

In a root that makes no election, `npm run features -- list` shows
   `continue-unfinished-turn` on, in core and in an exported instance
   (`npm test -- --only configuration-root`).

`docs/KIT.md` states the feature, its default and that it holds back
   only the end of a turn, once (`npm run test:docs`).
`npm test -- --review`, `npm test` and `npm run test:docs` pass.

criterion no reading can settle is recorded as such by the verifier, at its
own authority, the second time it comes back, and the repairing session is
told which ways out exist. A final review that finds a blocking defect
hands it back at the cost of one report.

   | a refuter's receipt for that text with a hold for the order | declines with a message that names the hold |
   | an order whose criterion differs from the text the refuter's receipt judged | declines with a message that names the criterion |

The re-cut command declines a criterion already re-cut once in the same
   order, with a message that names the defect record and the operator's
   amendment as what is left, and declines a criterion that the order's

criteria.text:
The route of an order whose final review has passed says whether its
   reviewed branches were published. Supported input: a fixture order
   closed by a passing final review and not merged; in the second and
   third rows it is a target order whose target worktree is registered.
   A fixture's log is written by the store's writer with the event the
   target publish records, and its ref by a push to the fixture's origin.
   Command:
   `npm test -- --only harness-fixtures`, the cases of
   `scripts/test-drive.mjs`.

   | --- | --- |

   | the order's branch was pushed, and the log holds one `PullRequestOpened` event that is no draft | the route stops as `awaiting-merge` |
   | a main checkout with no `origin`, and no remote-tracking ref for the order's branch | the route stops as `awaiting-merge` |
   | no remote-tracking ref for the order's branch, whose tip is an ancestor of `origin/main`, read with no events | the route stops as `awaiting-merge` |

   Control: the first two rows fail at the base, which stops as
   `awaiting-merge`. The other three pass there and must still pass; each
   fails under the planted fault that the route stops as
   `awaiting-publish` whenever the order is closed and not merged. The
   fifth is what the existing case that reads a merged branch with no
   events asserts, and that case's text is unchanged.

The emitted roots carry the reviewer's sentence and the router's stop.
   Command: `npm test -- --only harness-fixtures`, the case of
   `scripts/test-harness.mjs` that reads the emitted bundle.

   | Given | Then |
   | --- | --- |
   | the emitted `dotln-reviewer` root in each host directory the kit emits | each holds `A publish that a stop or the host declines is not tried again` |
   | the emitted `dotln-router` root in each host directory | each holds `awaiting-publish` |

   Control: both rows fail at the base.

A publish follows the level its root gives the stop
   `contribution-signoff`. Supported input: a branch holding one commit by
   an author the root does not name as its own, with no sign-off, in the
   fixture of `scripts/test-worktree.sh`, where no `gh` is on the path. A
   publish goes on when its output reaches
   `gh is required before any remote mutation`, which stands after the

   name, which the base's refusal does not hold, and the other three

The table of stops holds the row. Command:
   `npm test -- --only configuration-root`.

   | the same command in an exported instance's root | the row is at `advise` |

`plan start` under a labelled dispatch writes the pair record into the

orders.title: WO-207 — Instance update control: an instance takes kit machinery with its build pinned or followed, keeps its own code at a manifest-excluded extension root that the kit's machinery loads through the SourceAdapter port and no update touches, rolls back its last update to the prior kit state, and takes a starter update through the upgrade order its own planning pass cuts, or through the session-run route the README keeps for an instance owner without an order, gated by kit conformance and its own declared suites (version assigned at activation)
orders.objective:
An instance controls the kit updates it takes, from core and
inside the instance:

- **Its own code.** `dotln.config.json` may declare `extensions`: a root
  outside every kit tree (default `extensions/`) and adapters by kind
  (`source`, `effect`, `projection`). A vertical issue naming
  `source: "<id>"` has `prepare()` load that adapter, record
  `ExtensionLoaded { id, kind, path, sha256 }` and call its `fetchBundle`
  in place of `fetchIssueBundle`, with the bundle passing the same checks
  as the GitHub source's; `effect` and `projection` adapters are admitted
  and listed, never imported here. No export, manifest or update touches
  the root; the README states the review burden. The first consumer is a
  fixture adapter; an instance's own tracker adapter is that instance's.
- **Its build.** The kit manifest names its build (the compiled definition
  modules, their semantic hash and compiler version). An update takes
  `both` (today's), `machinery` (build modules kept at their pinned bytes,
  `build.pin` recorded, emit, check and `kit-verify` honoring it) or `build`
  (the build alone, then the re-emit), and refuses an incompatible pairing
  before any write; inside an instance, the upgrade order runs
  `build --pin` or `build --take` after its merge, as the channel the
  operator chose. WO-076's overlay composes over whichever build is pinned.
- **Its way back.** Each update logs what it did and keeps retained copies,
  refusing before any write when it cannot. `rollback` inside the instance,
  or `export --update <dir> --rollback` from core, returns the kit files
  and manifest to the logged state before the last update, reverses the
  reversible instance actions (the update's `build.pin` among them), lists
  the rest by id, logs itself and prints the re-emit, which the role that
  ran it runs next; it refuses, naming the path or row, after a later kit
  edit, when the update is not the latest, or when a prior file has no
  verified source.
- **Its way in.** An instance takes a starter update through the session-run
  route the client README records since WO-210: the incoming revision
  previewed from a detached worktree of that revision, the merge on an update
  branch, the re-emit and lineage index, one commit, the push and the update
  pull request the operator merges (the personal fork took its #1, #3, #8 and
  #16 this way). For the operator's instances the upgrade order a planning
  pass (dedicated, or part of one) cuts from the kit's template is that
  route's recorded form: it names the starter revision, the channel and each
  refused path's resolution, carries the route as its plan, runs the channel's
  `build` form after the merge and passes the gate below; the template's
  rollback form takes the way back the same way. A planning branch writes only
  `docs/` and root Markdown (WO-135), so the pass never applies kit files.
- **Its gate.** The consumer selection WO-213 decided (WO-213-D014: the six
  structural tasks and `kit-verify`, run fresh; carried kit suites stay
  explicit `--only` and `--machinery` diagnostics) plus the instance's own
  additions, the planner's proposal (assumption 8): suites it declares in
  `dotln.config.json` `suites` (name, command and sources), selected by
  changed sources, appended to that selection and run fresh, with each
  extension adapter naming the suite that covers it. Core's own gate is
  unchanged.
- **No step is the operator's by hand.** The operator gives the word (the
  starter revision, the channel, how each refused path resolves, a
  rollback), types the dispatch phrases and merges the pull request; a
  role runs every command and makes every commit (operator direction,
  2026-10-13; planning document §12.1).

## Goal-aligned decisions

The Contributor's purpose comes from [the vision](00-vision.md): DotLn is a
local-first, model-agnostic compiler/runtime for human judgment. This personal
implementation aims to improve operator flow by moving recurring supervision,
coordination, recovery and verification into dependable machinery, while
preserving correctness, authority, evidence, privacy and recoverability.

The current [critical-path plan](../planning/critical-path-2026-09-08.md) targets
the always-on runtime, its first real external source change and an independently
verified source-to-deliverable loop.

<!-- dotln-goal-rules:start -->

The [sequence](../planning/sequence.md) and selected work order determine
current placement and authority. The mission is the outcome; the critical path
is the dependency route to the next outcome. Useful prerequisite or
risk-reduction work must name the blocked outcome it enables. Process activity,
receipt volume and agent utilization are not progress by themselves. Goal
alignment grants no authority to reorder or expand work. In all phases, the Goal
Alignment and Process Cost procedure lives in the generated role skills
[WO-043, 2026-09-11].

Accuracy takes priority over agreement in every phase. The already-equipped
Correctness over Sycophancy rule applies to operator suggestions and the agent's
own premises equally: challenge unsupported claims, distinguish observation
from inference, state material uncertainty, and correct mistakes when evidence
changes. A confident request or an earlier decision is not proof of correctness.
Record material disagreement and its evidence in the same decision or phase
receipt; do not manufacture dissent or seek approval for ordinary judgment.

| Lens                                  | Decision question                                                                                         |
| ------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Policy resistance / fixes that fail   | Will local goals or guards undo one another?                                                              |
| Tragedy of the commons                | Does the solution consume shared compute, context or operator attention without accounting for the total? |
| Drift to low performance              | Does it improve an explicit outcome standard rather than normalize a worse baseline?                      |
| Escalation                            | Will additional process provoke more process or workarounds?                                              |
| Success to the successful             | Are credible alternatives excluded merely because the current mechanism already has investment?           |
| Shifting the burden to the intervenor | Does the solution remove recurring operator rescue or depend on it?                                       |
| Rule beating                          | Can the evidence pass without the intended behavior occurring?                                            |
| Seeking the wrong goal                | Does it advance operator flow and the selected product outcome rather than a proxy?                       |

Naive Interventionism adds the existing system's useful functions, affected
consumers, second-order harm, reversibility and smallest useful probe. NoOp
records what happens if nothing changes, why action or inaction wins, and the
evidence that would reopen the choice. Scale detail to consequence: explain
applicable risks and briefly group immaterial lenses with a reason; do not
manufacture eight repetitive paragraphs for routine edits.

Record evidence of benefit and the risks of intervening in existing behavior;
verification and handoff compare observed outcomes with the promised benefit.
Required legal or release actions retain their existing authority; NoOp is a
considered alternative, not an ambient veto or permission to abandon authorized
work.

<!-- dotln-goal-rules:end -->

**Platform lens.** Five checks from the platforms lesson the operator
pointed at (Steve Yegge's 2011 account of the Amazon service mandate) apply
to any capability a plan or order lands
[[vision-into-use pass](../planning/vision-into-use-2026-09-17.md) §12,
2026-09-17; [the 2026-11-16 pass](../planning/passes/the-kit-stops-no-work-2026-11-16.md#what-a-stop-protects-and-where-it-belongs)]:

- It arrives as an interface something else consumes (a transport profile,
  a typed event, a projection, a handoff packet), never only as a script or
  a session.
- It is externalizable by construction: content-addressed inputs, declared
  contracts, no private setting as the source of a guarantee.
- This repository and the operator's own repository consume it before any
  export.
- Its result is usable by a stranger to the session, so a receipt that
  needs reverse-engineering is an accessibility failure.
- An owner who is not the author can reach it on a machine that is not
  core's. One product is not right for everyone, so a stop, a fixed figure
  or a rule that such an owner cannot change fails this check before it
  protects anything.

Where reach and protection pull apart in an instance, a protection stays
on only where it guards what cannot be undone, and it stays the owner's to
lower. That does not make every stop useless: which ones earn their place
is judged stop by stop, from what each protects. The planning refuter's
platform-first standard is unchanged.

<!-- dotln-goal-rules:start -->

Material choices and rationales go in existing phase evidence: per-order
`docs/evidence/WO-NNN/decisions.md` and cited product sections for work-order
decisions; planning dispositions/candidate records for planning choices; the
independent report or refutation receipt for its judgment; retained closeout
evidence for release decisions. The decisions index exposes per-order records.
Reuse and link a current rationale until its assumptions change; do not create
a parallel decision log or an extra approval ritual.

<!-- dotln-goal-rules:end -->

The shared supports carry these duties and their compiled identity in both
harnesses. They are instruction-level judgment, not proof that an agent applied
every lens or a causal detector. The meter's five quantitative trap signals are
separate. General Naive Interventionism, NoOp and adaptive Tinkerer mechanics
retain their candidate scope; this bounded Contributor policy does not claim
their generalized implementations. The [WO-043 receipt](../evidence/WO-043/ideation-commands-and-usage.md)
records this promotion and its limits.

It holds the work order, the compiled subject (vision theses and exclusions, roles, capability rows, goal standard, critical-path table, five cost-table trap observations, the cost table and its acceptances, the first-verification fold, the seven judged orders and the sequence), the output instructions, the result schema and the worker instructions. I read no repository file and ran no command, search or Git operation. I spawned no agent and used no other tool, apart from writing result.json and this statement beside the prompt. The host also gave the session its standing instruction files and a repository status snapshot as context, and I did not use them as evidence. I judged WO-297, WO-291, WO-294, WO-289, WO-295, WO-296 and WO-298. Every order is aligned-with-findings, every finding is a known-issue with a reopening observation, there is no hold, and the plan verdict is aligned-with-findings. Model as the host reports it: claude-opus-5-5 (Opus 5.5). Effort is not read back by the host.

orders.criticalPathAndNoOp: The compiled order names no gate from the supplied critical-path table. The only table gate still in the sequence is P (WO-083, the fork's run). WO-297 reaches P only if the operator's instance declares a daily figure, and the subject does not show that it does (an inference, unverified). Its outcome is the mission's: once a figure is reached, a dispatched turn no longer ends and the operator no longer has to re-prompt. The records hold no NoOp cost for it. The cost table has no row for WO-297, because its rows were observed at c305d8ca on 2026-11-23, before this order existed, and costEvidenceStatus is stale. The shifting-the-burden observation shows 13 corrections and 4 directions at WO-287, 3 of them resumeDirection, but none is attributed to the daily figure. The NoOp cost is therefore unknown, not zero.
orders.systemTraps: Policy resistance: today the figure's turn-end works against the dispatch's duty to keep going. The order settles this in favour of keeping going and adds no guard, so it puts no pressure on guard refusals. Tragedy of the commons: material. The turn-end is the only behavior the compiled text attaches to a reached figure. Afterwards a reached figure is information only, so it no longer bounds a day's shared token spend, and the Cost line does not account for spend past the figure (finding 3). Drift to low performance: favourable. The executor root loses four bytes while it stands 57 bytes under its accepted ceiling (drift observation: 51,169 against 51,226). Escalation: it removes an instruction and adds no process. Success to the successful: the compiled text does not weigh the alternative of an owner-set level for the figure's effect. Shifting the burden: favourable. It removes the operator's recurring re-prompt after a figure-ended turn. Rule beating: material. Criterion 3 pins substrings, not the condition the turn-end clause applies under (finding 1). Seeking the wrong goal: it advances operator flow directly at a small process cost (three cases, one review run).
orders.removalBalance: Yes. The addition is text only: one sentence of the day's line and its comment, an executor-rule opening four bytes shorter, three expected texts, one generated row and two documentation passages. The removal is a behavioral instruction, taken out of every prompt past a reached figure in every instance that declares one. Root bytes fall overall. The day's line may change length, which is not stated, but that line sits in per-prompt facts, not in a root.
orders.failureBehavior: It fails without refusing, but it does not fall back to the old behavior. It adds no refusal (non-goal: any refusal). If the hook cannot compute the use or the figure, the line is absent and so is any turn-end instruction, so the session goes on as under the new behavior. Below the figure, the line holds neither new phrase (criterion 1, row 2). Not tested: whether a partial or stale line could still carry the old 'end the turn' wording after a read failure.

findings.reason: Rule beating. Row 1 requires the executor root to hold 'A day's figure' and the clause 'finish the step in hand, write docs/evidence/WO-NNN/standing.md and end the turn'. Row 2 forbids only 'say the day's figure is reached'. A rule reading 'A day's figure is reached: finish the step in hand, write ... and end the turn' passes both rows, yet it still tells the executor to end its turn at the figure, which is exactly what the objective removes. The criterion pins strings, not the condition under which the turn-end clause applies.
findings.reopenWhen: Either of two observations: the emitted dotln-executor root passes criterion 3 but holds a sentence that makes finishing the step, writing standing.md and ending the turn depend on the day's figure; or an executor session ends a turn citing a reached figure after the change.

findings.reason: One pass assigns the day's line to different orders. WO-297 changes the day's line and the opening of the executor rule. WO-298's non-goals say the day's figure belongs to WO-297. WO-289's non-goals still give 'the day's line of a prompt's facts and the executor's own sentence on ending a turn' to WO-288, which is sequenced between WO-297 and WO-289. If WO-288's filed criteria still assert the old line or sentence, either WO-297's change breaks them or WO-288's integration restores the old text.
findings.reopenWhen: WO-288's filed criteria or expected texts assert the day's line or the executor's turn-end sentence, or integrating WO-288 after WO-297 produces a conflict or reverts the day's line.

findings.reason: Tragedy of the commons, and the owner's reach. After the change, the compiled text gives a reached daily figure no behavioral effect, and the non-goals exclude any refusal. An owner who declared a figure to bound a day's spend loses that effect, with no level or rule to restore it. By contrast, WO-289 names how an owner removes its rule. The platform lens says a protection stays the owner's to set.

orders.criticalPathAndNoOp: No typed gate of the critical path names WO-288. The vision's one-paragraph story records the starter proof (WO-118, gate V's exit) complete; the sequence still holds WO-083 (gate P, the instance's own run under its emitted build) and WO-183 (the Teammate-ready rung, what-dotln-is-not:7). Part D (each of 139 limits keyed to a table an instance changes) and Part B5 (a core-only suite answers with its reason in an exported kit root) serve gate P and the platform lens's owner-reach check; Parts A, C, E and the rest of B are core-process risk reduction whose Cost line names removals but no blocked outcome, which the goal card asks every prerequisite to name. NoOp in the records: the cost table's WO-288 row has null metrics and no trap series reaches it. Its own record in the WO-288 worktree is the largest process datum of this horizon, checked here: docs/control/orders/WO-288.jsonl holds 11 VerificationCompleted events, all fail, and 10 RepairCompleted, with requested-to-completed sums of 8 h 22 min of verification and 48 h 6 min of repair, and the Process cost lines of docs/verifications/WO-288/VER-001.md to VER-011.md sum to 335.8 million handoff tokens. Doing nothing about its scope would keep fixed limits an instance cannot change (a platform-lens failure), the copied critic launcher and the hand-kept timer, and the planning check's memory cost, which the Cost line puts at about 2 GiB per run and E1 has yet to measure.
orders.systemTraps: Policy resistance: criterion 23 (D1) came back in 10 of 11 verifications (VER-005 alone met it), on varying paths across rounds (for example an expiring wait, a listed limit that bounds nothing, reads that end at the figure without key or file, four paths in VER-011), so the table and its up to 327 consuming sites kept undoing one another across repairs. Tragedy of the commons: about 62 worker uses by the Cost line plus a critic every 75 minutes at 15 to 20 minutes each, against a shared subagent cap that one acceptance covers; the record adds 335.8 million verification tokens. Drift to low performance: the emitted roots in the WO-288 worktree measure executor 54,493, verifier 44,577, reviewer 48,107 and planner 35,139 bytes (CLAUDE.md plus each skill, measured here) against ceilings of 51,226, 42,811, 45,385 and 34,876 from the drift series, while the Cost line names four changed sentences and Z1's frame rules and no cold-start budget. Escalation: the order adds a critic, a critic of the critics and a fourth disposition word, and the WO-288 worktree's order text has grown from these 33 criteria to 41 (Part F) during execution. Success to the successful: bundling five parts to save two activations, verifications, final reviews and releases was preferred to separate orders; the record shows eleven verifications, so the alternative was not shown worse. Shifting the burden to the intervenor: Part D and the critic's points by class remove recurring operator rescue in principle; the shifting-the-burden series rose to 13 corrections and 4 directions at WO-287, the last measured order. Rule beating: E2 passes on a halved peak or on a recorded negative, and C3 on ready, negative or inconclusive, so the evidence can pass while the named removal does not occur. Seeking the wrong goal: most parts are machinery for core's own sessions; only Part D and B5 reach an instance owner.
orders.removalBalance: No, not as observed. The additions are a kinds module and section, launch and due commands, a transcript screen, a transport request kind, a second charter, the points' record, the review helper's reader and merge, the bound error's fields, a key for each of 139 limits read at up to 327 sites, a measuring script and advisories, roughly 50 to 60 cases and about 62 worker uses. The removals are the copied launcher, the hand-kept timer, the critic's Codex dependence, a lost round record, two mis-launched rounds, an instance probe failure, an intermittent complete-run loss, a fixed figure at each limit site, about 2 GiB and half a minute per planning check, and two of three activations, verifications, final reviews and releases. Only Part E's per-check saving and Part D's owner reach recur; Part E's size is unmeasured until E1 and may close negative under E2. The bundling saving is contradicted by the record (eleven verifications and ten repairs, not one verification). The removal is therefore not shown larger than the addition; tokens and steps are unknown by the Cost line's own statement.
orders.failureBehavior: Mostly degrades. With features.critic-cadence absent or off, due names nothing and neither hook adds a line (A4), which is the exported instance's default (Z2); a malformed kinds row is one advisory and the kit's row launches (A2); a standing file's age, a left to-fix point and a planning-check reader miss are advisories that refuse nothing (A6, A10, E5); a malformed checks file reads as unavailable without a throw (A7); with enforce false a limit ends nothing (D1). Refusals remain only on malformed input or a leak: a screened transcript withholds the critic launch (A3); a report without a table, a first-round launch naming a report and a receipt typed dotln-worker-fable are refused with reasons (B1 to B3) while an earlier receipt still reads; an exported kit root's core-only suite exits nonzero with a distinct status (B5). The non-goals exclude any new refusal in Part E and any stop an instance cannot lower.
